title: Regional spillover & SLA-aware model fallback notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects pragmatic architecture notes and an operational runbook for SLA-aware fallbacks and regional spillover. Focus areas: routing policies at the control plane, model-variant selection logic, tiered capacity handling, and safe spillover between regions (and between Dedicated/Hosted pools). Intended for platform engineers, SRE, and solutions engineers designing production routing behavior.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Keep high-priority traffic within SLA targets (p99 latency, availability objectives) while minimizing cost.
- Provide deterministic fallback behavior when preferred model/region is unavailable.
- Avoid cascading failures during spikes (circuit-breaker + rate-limited spillover).
- Make policies auditable and tunable from the control plane.

Key concepts and vocabulary:
- Primary region: region that owns the customer’s affinity/endpoint.
- Backup region: pre-authorized region to receive spillover traffic for a customer.
- Model variant: semantically equivalent model with different cost/latency profile (e.g., full_fp16, q4_K_MN, or distil).
- Capacity tier: bucketed compute class (reserved-dedicated, burst-dedicated, hosted-lowpri, hosted-on-demand).
- SLA class: customer-defined tolerance profile: "gold", "silver", "bronze" with mapping to latency and cost priorities.
- Control plane policy: declarative rule attached to customer or route that drives routing/fallback decisions.

High-level policy design (control plane primitives):
- route.selector: static attributes (customer_id, route_id, region_prefs).
- route.sla_class: gold | silver | bronze. Maps to ordered fallback policy and allowed capacity tiers.
- route.model_family: canonical model name (semantics). Fallback list: ordered model_variants with thresholds.
- route.region_policy: { primary, backups: [r2, r3], spill_limit: X per_minute, max_latency_overhead_ms } as strings in the UI.
- route.fallback_conditions: numeric thresholds that trigger fallback (queue_length > T, avg_latency_ms > L, error_rate > E, available_slots < S).
- route.degradation_profile: per-sla maps of allowed quality reduction steps (e.g., tolerate distil -> quantized -> cached-response).

Example declarative fallback sequence (gold SLA):
1) preferred: primary region, model_variant: full_fp16 on reserved-dedicated.
2) if reserved-dedicated saturated for > 3s or latency > 150ms p99: fall back to burst-dedicated same region.
3) if region-level failure or sustained overload: spillover to backup region r2 using full_fp16 on burst-dedicated (rate-limited to 20 qps/customer).
4) if remote region not available or cost constraint: switch model_variant to q4_K_MN (lower latency/cost trade) in r2.
5) final fallback: hosted-on-demand distil model with user-facing notice (for interactive applications) and telemetry flag.

Tiered capacity mapping examples (policy defaults):
- reserved-dedicated: capacity >= 90% SLA guarantee, high cost.
- burst-dedicated: ephemeral capacity, limited seconds/minutes per burst policy.
- hosted-on-demand: best-effort, no SLA, used for last-resort fallbacks.
- hosted-lowpri: cheapest, used for low-priority batch jobs/embeddings.

Decision logic and scoring function (sketch):
We evaluate candidate endpoints (region+capacity+model_variant) with a score = w1*(latency_headroom_ms) + w2*(cost_penalty) + w3*(freshness_penalty) + w4*(sla_violation_risk). Select highest score above threshold. We implement as an ordered filter + scoring tie-breaker in the control plane for deterministic results.

Control plane implementation notes:
- Policies are stored as small JSON blobs attached to Org or Route config. Use explicit schema versioning.
- Evaluation should be idempotent and fast (< 2ms in-path decision), ideally evaluated in the gateway routing tier with cached agent tokens that refresh every few seconds.
- Fallback evaluation must consider in-flight requests and queue depth; avoid per-request re-evaluations that thrash. Use short-lived leases on endpoints.

Operational runbook (short form):
Signals that should trigger automated fallback:
- Node or rack outage in primary region (node health check fails).
- p99 latency exceeding configured threshold for > sliding_window_seconds (default 10s).
- CPU/GPU queue depth > threshold (backpressure metric).
- Error rate spike (5xx) > X% for > 30s.
Automated actions in order:
1) Open circuit for the affected pool (stop new assignments to that pool).
2) Promote burst capacity if available in same region.
3) Begin controlled spillover to backup region at configured spill_limit.
4) If backups not available, apply model-variant degradation steps per SLA class.
5) Notify on-call channel and populate incident context with policy decisions.
6) If fallback reduces quality (e.g., distillation), emit customer-visible telemetry and an incident action item to follow up.

Example incident timeline (template):
- t0: spike detected: p99 latency 220ms (gold SLA threshold 150ms).
- t0+12s: open circuit on reserved-dedicated pool.
- t0+20s: route traffic to burst-dedicated in primary region. p99 ~ 170ms.
- t0+45s: traffic exceeds burst burst_limit; begin 10 qps/customer spillover to r2.
- t0+90s: r2 uses quantized variant under cost cap; p99 restored to 140ms.
- t0+6h: capacity provisioning completed; route moved back to reserved-dedicated.

Observability and alerting:
- Expose policy decision traces for each routed request (reason code: capacity_saturated | region_unavailable | degradation_applied). Keep sampled traces (1:1000) for storage cost control.
- Metrics to emit: fallback_rate, spillover_rate_by_region, model_variant_switch_rate, per-route sla_violation_time_seconds, rollback_count.
- Alerts: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m on gold routes; spillover_rate > X leads to paging.

Testing and verification checklist:
- Unit tests for decision engine with simulated capacity and latency metrics.
- Integration test harness that simulates region outage and validates: no data-loss, fallbacks honored, rollback path works.
- Chaos test (limited blast radius): randomly fail N nodes in primary region for a small set of test-orgs and verify policies.
- Load test: ramp to 2x expected peak and ensure spillover + model degradation preserves p99 for gold routes.

Customer controls and UX decisions:
- Expose simple toggles in Console: enable_region_spillover (bool), preferred_backup_regions (ordered list), max_remote-cost-per-token (numeric).
- For enterprise orgs: support explicit allowlist of backup regions (required for data residency). If not allowed, fallback must be model-only (quantize/distill) within primary region.
- For hosted public customers: default allowlist includes nearby regions for latency reasons.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we allow cross-tenant borrowing of reserved capacity for emergencies (with strict accounting)? Pros: faster recovery. Cons: noisy-neighbor risk and billing complexity.
- How to represent multi-hop fallbacks (region -> model_variant -> cache) to make decisions reversible and auditable?
- What are cost accounting signals needed to enforce per-org remote-cost caps effectively?

Short-term action items (owner initials):
- Asha: prototype scoring function and add schema v0.2 to control plane config. (ETA: 2024-10-02)
- Diego: add fallback decision trace instrumentation to gateway. (ETA: 2024-10-15)
- Mei: run chaos experiment design and scheduling with SRE. (ETA: 2024-11-01)
- Evan: compile cost impact model for quantized vs distil variants for marketing/pricebook. (ETA: 2024-10-08)

Appendix: example policy blob (human-friendly form)
- route_id: cust-42/chat-main
- sla_class: gold
- primary_region: us-west1
- backups: [us-central1, us-east1]
- spill_limit_per_minute: 120
- model_family: redwood-chat-v2
- model_variants_order: [full_fp16, q4_K_MN, distil-v2]
- degradation_windows: [ {step: q4_K_MN, min_seconds: 30}, {step: distil-v2, min_seconds: 120} ]
- allowed_capacity_tiers: [reserved-dedicated, burst-dedicated, hosted-on-demand]

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep fallback logic conservative by default, surface aggressive policies behind opt-in flags.
- We should discuss a billing-side SLA credit model for cross-region spillover since remote regions increase egress and peak costs.
- Remember to sync with Solutions Eng before changing default backups for enterprise customers.

End of doc.
